chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the interpretation of 'In the Name of God, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful.' He said: 'The Ba is the Splendor (Baha') of God, and the Sin is the Sublimity (Sana') of God, and the Mim is the Glory (Majd) of God.'

And some of them narrated: 'The Mim is the Kingdom (Mulk) of God. And God is the God of everything; the All-beneficent toward all His creation, and the All-merciful toward the believers in particular.'

key_terms.الرَّحِيمُ بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ خَاصَّةً: ar-Rahim — specifically and particularly merciful to the believers
key_terms.الرَّحْمَنُ بِجَمِيعِ خَلْقِهِ: ar-Rahman — universally merciful to all creation without exception
key_terms.بَهَاءُ اللَّهِ: Baha' Allah — The Splendor/Radiance of God; Ba is the letter standing for this divine attribute
key_terms.سَنَاءُ اللَّهِ: Sana' Allah — The Sublimity/Exaltedness of God; Sin stands for this divine attribute
key_terms.مَجْدُ اللَّهِ: Majd Allah — The Glory of God; Mim stands for this in the primary narration
key_terms.مُلْكُ اللَّهِ: Mulk Allah — The Kingdom/Sovereignty of God; Mim stands for this in the alternate narration

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say is the esoteric meaning of Bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Rahim?
ai.summary: Abdullah ibn Sinan, a trusted companion of Imam al-Sadiq (AS), reports asking the Imam about the esoteric meaning of the Basmala — 'Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim.' The Imam provided a letter-by-letter interpretation of the word 'Bism': Ba for Baha' (Divine Splendor), Sin for Sana' (Divine Sublimity), and Mim for Majd (Divine Glory), with an alternate tradition interpreting Mim as Mulk (Divine Kingdom). He also distinguished between ar-Rahman, which denotes God's universal mercy encompassing all creation, and ar-Rahim, which signifies a special mercy reserved exclusively for the believers (mu'minun). This kind of esoteric letter-by-letter hermeneutic (ta'wil) is a hallmark of the interpretive tradition preserved by Imam al-Sadiq's circle in the 8th century CE.
